title: A Direct Detector Can Measure and Monochromate the Energy of Backscattered Electrons
content: While high voltage Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEMs) can be equipped with energy filters [1] for electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) and energy filtered TEM imaging (EFTEM), such equipment is not compatible with scanning electron microscopes (SEMs). This is because the scanned beam is typically backscattered at large angles, SEMs are typically not built with a port to accommodate such a filter, SEMs have no post-specimen optics to re-focus the beam towards such a filter, and lastly because commercial energy filters are more expensive than most SEMs. The lack of an SEM energy filter has stopped techniques such as band-gap measurements, and monochromated imaging, from being possible in an SEM. EFTEM imaging contributes significantly to resolution improvement in cryo electron microscopy, with most high end cryo TEMs now using an energy filter [2].
